rules: Layer 8 (assets/provinces.json) is the only source of territorial geometry for Region.
The hierarchy is authored bottom-up only. This version intentionally contains Region only; C/V/B are disabled until they are rebuilt from verified Regions.
Region may contain only explicit stable province_ids from layer 8; no centroid, bbox, nearest-neighbour, coordinate or shape guessing is allowed.
No Region may carry its own polygon/rings/bbox/coordinates geometry.
A layer-8 province may belong to one Region only.
A historical Region may not mix provinces from different countries.
Historical/geographical correctness has priority over the target size of 3-4 provinces. One-province and 5+ province Regions are allowed when the source requires them.
If a layer-8 province is too coarse to reproduce a finer historical boundary safely, Province = Region is allowed temporarily rather than forcing a historically false union.
Every authored Region must record internet sources and a historical_basis. Game convenience is never a valid basis.
Unverified world areas remain absent from X instead of being guessed.
Higher tiers must later be derived only from this Region layer and independently verified before C/V/B are enabled.

coverage.note: This pass replaces the previous Iberian X layer only. Other layer-8 world provinces are intentionally left unassigned until their Regions are researched country by country.

groups.historical_basis: España regional (IGN, 1910) treats Galicia as a historical region. At the layer-8 provincial scale it is exactly La Coruña, Lugo, Orense and Pontevedra; no Portuguese territory is included.
Asturias is a separate Region in España regional (IGN, 1910). Layer 8 currently has one Asturias province, so Province = Region is exact at the available granularity.
The IGN 1912 geographic review explicitly states that the old Kingdom/Region of León comprises León, Zamora and Salamanca.

Castilla la Vieja is one of the explicit historical Regions in the IGN 1910 regional atlas. The current layer-8 La Rioja and Cantabria polygons stand for the historical Logroño and Santander provincial territories at this scale. The eight-province size is retained because historical correctness overrides the 3-4 target average.
The IGN 1912 review explicitly defines Castilla la Nueva as Ciudad Real, Cuenca, Guadalajara, Madrid and Toledo.
The IGN 1912 review explicitly defines Extremadura as Cáceres and Badajoz.
España regional (IGN, 1910) has Vascongadas as a separate northern Region. The 1810 IGN atlas identifies the Provincias Bascongadas as Vizcaya, Guipúzcoa and Álava. Navarra remains a separate Region.
Navarra is a separate Region in the IGN 1910 regional atlas and a separate kingdom in the 1810 atlas. Layer 8 contains it as one province, so Province = Region.
Aragón is a separate historical Region in the IGN 1910 atlas; the layer-8 provinces Zaragoza, Huesca and Teruel reproduce the standard provincial composition.
Cataluña is a separate historical Region in the IGN 1910 atlas. Layer 8 uses Barcelona, Tarragona, Lérida/Lleida and Gerona/Girona.
The IGN 1912 review explicitly defines Valencia as Castellón, Valencia and Alicante.
The IGN 1912 review explicitly defines the historical Murcia Region as Murcia and Albacete.

España regional (IGN, 1910) treats Andalucía as one Region. The IGN 1912 review records its four historical kingdoms and their provinces: Sevilla = Cádiz, Huelva, Sevilla; Córdoba = Córdoba; Jaén = Jaén; Granada = Almería, Granada, Málaga. Their union therefore gives exactly the eight layer-8 Andalusian provinces, without the previous arbitrary western/eastern split.
Baleares is a separate Region in the IGN 1910 regional atlas. Layer 8 currently represents the archipelago as one province, so Province = Region.
Canarias is a separate Region in the IGN regional classification. Layer 8 uses the later two-province subdivision, which is reunited only at Region level.

Portugal has well-attested historical provinces, but their boundaries do not safely coincide with every modern layer-8 district. Until layer 8 is subdivided more finely, this district remains Province = Region rather than being silently swallowed by an approximate historical polygon.
Temporary Province = Region fallback at current layer-8 district granularity. Historical Minho is verified, but no approximate cross-district union is used until exact subdivision is available.
Temporary Province = Region fallback. The historical Douro/Entre-Douro-e-Minho boundary history makes a whole modern Porto district unsafe to merge without finer layer-8 subdivision.
Temporary Province = Region fallback. Trás-os-Montes is historically verified, but the current layer-8 district geometry is retained unchanged until exact historical subdivision is implemented.
Temporary Province = Region fallback at current layer-8 granularity; no coordinate or nearest-neighbour assignment is allowed.

Temporary Province = Region fallback. Aveiro lies in an area whose historical provincial affiliations changed; the whole modern layer-8 district is therefore not forced into an approximate historical Region.
Temporary Province = Region fallback because historical Beira/Douro boundaries cannot be reproduced exactly by the current whole Coimbra district polygon.
Viseu was the capital of historical Beira Alta in the nineteenth-century eight-province system. Layer 8 is retained as one district Region until finer subdivision is available.
Temporary Province = Region fallback. Historical Beira boundaries are source-backed, but the whole modern Guarda district is not assigned by approximation.

Castelo Branco was the capital of historical Beira Baixa in the nineteenth-century eight-province system. The current district remains Province = Region rather than expanding beyond its exact layer-8 polygon.
Temporary Province = Region fallback. Leiria's historical provincial affiliations cannot be reproduced safely from the unsplit whole layer-8 district.
Lisboa is the historical capital associated with Estremadura, but the exact historical Region is not approximated from whole modern districts. Province = Region is retained temporarily.
Temporary Province = Region fallback; the current layer-8 district is kept intact until an exact source-backed subdivision can reproduce historical Estremadura/Ribatejo boundaries.
Temporary Province = Region fallback because the current Setúbal district cannot be assigned wholesale to a historical province without risking a boundary error.
Temporary Province = Region fallback. Alentejo is historically verified, but no unsafe whole-district approximation is introduced.
Évora is the historical capital associated with Alentejo in the eight-province system. The layer-8 district is kept as Province = Region until finer historical borders exist.
Temporary Province = Region fallback at current layer-8 granularity; future subdivision may place it inside an exact historical Alentejo Region.
Algarve is one of the long-standing traditional/historical Portuguese provinces. At current layer-8 granularity Faro is retained as Region Algarve.
Madeira is an insular Portuguese historical/geographical territory distinct from mainland provinces. Layer 8 represents it as one province, so Province = Region.
The Azores are an insular Portuguese historical/geographical territory distinct from mainland provinces. Layer 8 represents the archipelago as one province, so Province = Region.
